critical_code_review_comments: setupScrollReveal() applies .reveal class via JS and observes via IntersectionObserver - works but fragile: any future structural section added with intended reveal animation must also be added to the targets selector. Consider inverting: query [data-reveal] attribute on elements that opt in, or simply query '.reveal' class already in HTML. Currently the .alert-note has class 'reveal' hardcoded in HTML but JS overwrites/re-adds it; risk of similar bugs if other sections get class='reveal' in HTML but are not in the JS selector list.
Accessibility-mode toggle correctly bypasses scroll-reveal by adding .is-visible to all .reveal elements - good fallback.
No data-testid attributes on interactive elements (accordion triggers, accessibility toggle, openBooking buttons). Recommended for future automation.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Static site served by /app/frontend/serve.js on port 3000 from /app/static-website/. Backend supervisor service is in BACKOFF state intentionally - ignore. The .alert-note bug fix is in script.js setupScrollReveal() targets selector (line 104). All 5 subpages share same script.js, so fix is universal.
rca of the issue: RCA: The .alert-note element had class='reveal' in HTML (opacity:0 via CSS) but was NOT in the IntersectionObserver targets selector in setupScrollReveal(). Therefore no observer was attached and 'is-visible' class was never added, leaving the element permanently at opacity:0 (only the colored background was visible). Fix: added '.alert-note' to the targets querySelectorAll selector. Verified via Playwright on all 5 subpages - element now reaches opacity ~0.98 and is-visible class is applied after scroll into view.
